column1: # Baseline tools and optional-module packages: the single source of truth for every platform.
# Columns (tab-separated, use "-" for an empty field):
#   name    unique key; a row in manifest/local/baseline.tsv with the same key replaces this one
#   check   how presence is detected: a command, "a|b" for alternatives, "app:Name" for /Applications/Name.app,
#           "lib:soname" for a shared library the dynamic linker knows (Linux)
#   group   baseline (installed by --apply) or the optional module that installs it
#   macos   brew:<formula> | cask:<cask> | npm:<package> | os (shipped with macOS) | - (not applicable)
#   debian  Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 12 (x86_64): apt:<package>[|<alternative>...] | apt-repo:<repo>:<package> (repo from apt-repos.tsv) |
#           npm:<package> | installer:<official install.sh URL> | uv-python:<version> | uv-tool:<tool> |
#           orca-deb:<owner/repo>:<package> (.deb from the latest stable GitHub release) |
#           github-release:<owner/repo>:<asset>:<command> (a single-file binary from the latest stable GitHub
#           release, checked against GitHub's sha256 digest and installed as ~/.local/bin/<command>) | -
# On Debian, --apply installs apt packages first (curl, gnupg and certificates are needed to add the
# third-party repositories), then repositories, official installers, npm packages and uv-managed tools, and
# finally the Orca .deb (its download is read with node).
# Electron needs these libraries, but the Orca .deb does not depend on them (electron-builder's default list lacks
# them), so a minimal server or container cannot start orca-ide without them. "a|b" installs the first package
# the distribution has: Ubuntu 24.04 ships libasound2t64, Debian 12 libasound2.
# Docker Engine on Linux: the packages of Docker's own install guide, from its apt repository (apt-repos.tsv).
# --containers leaves Docker or Podman from any other source alone (apt-conflicts.tsv).
# On Linux android-sdk-platform-tools is a metapackage that only recommends adb and fastboot (--apply installs
# without recommends), so they are rows of their own.
